summary: Revised migration: add customer_note column, copy data, deploy new app, retire old app, drop note column, with bidirectional sync trigger to ensure cross-version consistency during overlap.
write_consistency: Old app writes to note, new app writes to customer_note; a bidirectional PL/pgSQL trigger syncs both columns on every INSERT/UPDATE, ensuring both versions read the most recently written value.
revision_notes: Root cause: the previous plan had no synchronization mechanism between the note and customer_note columns. Since the old app writes to note and the new app writes to customer_note, cross-version reads observed stale seed data or null instead of the expected value, causing all 16 consistency checks to fail during deploy_new. Revised plan adds a bidirectional sync trigger in the expand stage that keeps note and customer_note aligned with the most recent write from either version.

stages.description: Add customer_note column, copy data, and add sync trigger
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_user_note() RETURNS trigger AS \$\$ BEGIN NEW.note := COALESCE(NEW.note, NEW.customer_note); NEW.customer_note := COALESCE(NEW.customer_note, NEW.note); RETURN NEW; END; \$\$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_note AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_user_note();

stages.description: Deploy the new app version (new-staged) which now reads and writes the customer_note column.
Retire the old app version (old) that still uses the note column; after retirement the note column is removed.

sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
